name: Multi-Projection Coherence Governance Registry

core_rule.name: projection_agreement_not_identity_rule
core_rule.definition: Agreement between multiple projections may indicate shared source consistency, but it does not reconstruct or prove the full ⇔R source relation.

coherence_classes.name: shared_trace_coherence
coherence_classes.definition: Multiple projections retain compatible source_relation pointers.

coherence_classes.name: feature_overlap_coherence
coherence_classes.definition: Multiple projections retain compatible reduced features from the same source relation.

coherence_classes.name: loss-aware_partial_coherence
coherence_classes.definition: Projection agreement exists, but major or critical features remain lost.

coherence_classes.name: projection_conflict
coherence_classes.definition: Projected forms produce incompatible retained-feature claims or inconsistent source metadata.

governance_rules.rule: Multiple projections may be compared only when they declare the same source_relation or explicitly governed source-link.
Projection agreement cannot be treated as reconstruction of the source relation.
Conflicting retained features must be recorded rather than collapsed.
The union of lost features must be tracked for all compared projections.
Multi-projection coherence cannot promote physics, arithmetic, or theorem claims.

forbidden_claims: Projection agreement proves the source relation.
Multiple projections reconstruct ⇔R by convergence alone.
QM-like and GR-like projection agreement proves unification.
Arithmetic-like projection agreement replaces standard arithmetic.
Conflicting projection features can be ignored.
Projection coherence is theorem evidence by default.
